record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory
record.original_question: For fixed metric spaces or Banach spaces X and Y, is the family of sets B_C(X,Y) of Hölder exponents for C-distorted extension continuous as a function of the distortion constant C?

evidence.quote: for C ≥ 1, BC(X, Y ) denotes the set of all α ∈ (0, 1] such that any (K, α)-H¨older function f from a subset of X into Y can be extended to a (CK, α)-H¨older function from X into Y .
Problem 5.3. Is the collection of sets BC(X, Y ) continuous with respect to C?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be metric spaces (or Banach spaces). For a constant $C \geq 1$, define $B_C(X,Y) \subseteq (0,1]$ to be the set of all exponents $\alpha \in (0,1]$ with the following extension property: for every subset $A \subseteq X$, every $K > 0$, and every map $f \colon A \to Y$ satisfying
$$d_Y(f(x), f(y)) \le K\, d_X(x,y)^\alpha \quad \text{for all } x,y \in A,$$
there exists an extension $\tilde f \colon X \to Y$ of $f$ such that
$$d_Y(\tilde f(x), \tilde f(y)) \le CK\, d_X(x,y)^\alpha \quad \text{for all } x,y \in X.$$
Thus $\{B_C(X,Y)\}_{C \geq 1}$ is a family of subsets of $(0,1]$, increasing in $C$.

Question: For fixed $X$ and $Y$, is the set-valued map $C \mapsto B_C(X,Y)$ continuous in $C \in [1,\infty)$? Equivalently, does one have
$$B_C(X,Y) = \bigcap_{C' > C} B_{C'}(X,Y) \quad \text{and} \quad B_C(X,Y) = \overline{\bigcup_{C' < C} B_{C'}(X,Y)}\text{ (in an appropriate sense)}$$
for every $C \geq 1$?
artifact.category_tag: Hölder extension of maps between metric spaces
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any paper resolving the continuity of the family $B_C(X,Y)$ as a function of the distortion constant $C$. Related literature addresses isometric ($C=1$) and general Hölder extension problems with values in $C(K)$ or $c_0$, but does not appear to address continuity of $B_C(X,Y)$ in $C$. The status therefore cannot be confirmed from the available sources.

status_evidence.title: On the extension of Hölder maps with values in spaces of continuous functions
status_evidence.snippet: For a finite dimensional normed space X and for a compact metric space K, the set of α's for which all α-Hölder maps from a subset of X into C(K) can be extended isometrically is either (0,1] or (0,1).
status_evidence.claim: Related work studies the set of admissible Hölder exponents for extension, but does not address continuity in the distortion constant C.
